item.title: Gion Guide: Kyoto's Geisha District & How to Visit Respectfully
item.description: Gion is Kyoto’s most famous geisha district — a maze of wooden machiya townhouses, paper-lantern-lit lanes, exclusive tea houses, and willow-lined canals, where the city’s living traditions of music, dance, and hospitality have continued for centuries. At dusk, when the lanterns glow and a geiko (Kyoto’s word for geisha) or maiko (apprentice) hurries to an evening engagement, Gion feels like stepping into another era. It is also a real, working neighbourhood where over-tourism and disrespectful behaviour have caused genuine problems — to the point that some private lanes now ban photography entirely.
